title: Set 68

sentences.ko: 이번 주말에 데크에 페인트 칠하려고 했는데 일요일까지 계속 비 온대. 젖은 나무 위에는 페인트를 못 칠하잖아. 그래서 페인트 통은 그냥 차고에 놓여 있고, 이제 이틀이 통째로 비었는데 그 이틀에 아무것도 안 할 거라는 걸 벌써 알아.
sentences.text: We were going to paint the deck this weekend, but they're saying rain right through Sunday, and you can't paint over wet wood. So the cans are just sitting in the garage, and now I've got two free days and I already know I'm not going to do anything with them.

alts.text: Supposed to paint the deck this weekend, but they're calling for rain right through Sunday, and you can't paint wet wood. So the cans are just sitting in the garage, and now I've got two free days and I already know I'm not gonna do a thing with them.

We had planned to paint the deck this weekend, but the forecast calls for rain through Sunday, and one cannot paint over wet wood. The cans are therefore sitting in the garage, and I now have two free days that I already know I will not do anything with.

sentences.note: **they're saying rain** 는 일기예보에서 비 온다고 한다는 뜻입니다. casual 의 **they're calling for rain** 도 똑같은 말이고, 날씨 얘기할 때 주어를 they 로 두는 게 자연스럽습니다.

sentences.ko: 물 달라고 두 번 부르더니, 그다음엔 복도 불을 켜 놔야 한다고 하고, 그다음엔 지난주에 꾼 꿈 얘기를 해야겠다는 거야. 그래서 벌써 열 시가 다 됐는데 나는 아직도 애 침대 끝에 앉아서 휴대폰을 엎어 놓고 있어. 화면 보이면 이십 분은 더 안 잘 테니까. 오늘 밤은 진이 다 빠졌어.
sentences.text: He asked for water twice, and then he needed the hallway light on, and then he wanted to tell me about a dream he had last week. So it's almost ten and I'm still on the edge of his bed with my phone face down, because if he sees the screen we're up another twenty minutes. I've got nothing left tonight.

alts.text: Two rounds of water, then the hallway light had to be on, then he had to tell me about some dream he had last week. So it's almost ten and I'm still parked on the edge of his bed with my phone face down, because if he spots the screen we're up another twenty minutes. I'm done tonight.

He asked for water twice, then required the hallway light to be left on, and then wished to tell me about a dream he had last week. It is nearly ten and I am still sitting on the edge of his bed with my phone face down, because if he sees the screen we will be awake another twenty minutes. I have nothing left this evening.

sentences.note: **my phone face down** 은 불빛이 새어 나가지 않게 휴대폰을 화면이 바닥으로 가게 엎어 두는 것입니다. casual 의 **I'm done tonight** 은 오늘은 더 못 버티겠다, 기운이 다 떨어졌다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 온수가 오 분쯤 지나면 찬물로 바뀌어서, 우리 셋이 매일 아침 그 전에 끝내려고 후다닥 씻어요. 제가 너무 오래 틀어 놓나 싶어서 바로 연락은 안 드렸는데, 아래층 여자분은 작년에 온수기를 갈아 줬다고 하더라고요. 사람 좀 보내서 봐 주실 수 있을까요? 목요일에 집에 있고, 그 뒤로는 아무 날이나 오전에 있어요.
sentences.text: The hot water goes cold about five minutes in, so the three of us are rushing through showers every morning trying to beat it. I held off on calling because I figured maybe I was just running it too long, but the woman downstairs said they replaced her heater last year. Can you get somebody out to look at it? I'm home Thursday, or any morning after that.

alts.text: About five minutes in, the hot water just quits, so all three of us are racing through showers every morning trying to beat it. I didn't call sooner because I figured maybe I was just running it too long, but the woman downstairs said they swapped out her heater last year. Any chance you can send someone out to look at it? I'm home Thursday, or any morning after that.

The hot water turns cold after approximately five minutes, so the three of us hurry through our showers each morning in order to finish before it runs out. I refrained from calling because I assumed I might simply be running it too long, but the woman downstairs told me that her heater was replaced last year. Could you arrange for someone to come and look at it? I am home on Thursday, or any morning thereafter.

sentences.note: **I held off on calling** 은 연락할까 하다가 바로 하지 않고 미뤘다는 말입니다. casual 의 **swapped out** 은 기기나 부품을 통째로 새것으로 갈아 끼웠다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 집주인이랑 고장 난 것 고쳐 달라고 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 가방까지 다 싸 놓고 퇴근하면서 바로 헬스장 가려고 했는데, 집에 먼저 들렀거든. 그래서 운동화가 아직 회사 책상 밑에 그대로 있어. 그거 가지러 여섯 시에 시내까지 다시 운전해 가진 않을 거니까 오늘 저녁은 날아간 거지. 아침에 갈게. 매번 그렇게 말하는 거 나도 알아.
sentences.text: I had my bag packed and I was going straight to the gym from work, but I came home first, and now my shoes are still sitting under my desk at work. And I'm not driving back downtown at six for them, so that's tonight gone. I'll go in the morning, which I know I say every time.

alts.text: Bag was packed, I was heading straight to the gym from work, but I stopped home first, and now my shoes are still under my desk at the office. And I'm not driving back downtown at six just for those, so there goes tonight. I'll go in the morning. Yeah, I say that every time.

I had packed my bag and intended to go directly to the gym from work, but I came home first, and my shoes are still sitting under my desk at the office. I am not going to drive back downtown at six to retrieve them, so this evening is lost. I will go in the morning, though I am aware that I say that every time.

sentences.note: **so that's tonight gone** 은 오늘 저녁 계획이 그냥 날아갔다는 뜻입니다. casual 의 **there goes tonight** 도 같은 말인데, there goes 는 눈앞에서 뭔가 사라질 때 흔히 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 운동 가려다 말게 된 핑계 대기

sentences.ko: 동생이 또 돈 빌려 달라고 하더라. 돈이 없어서가 아니라, 지난번에 빌려 간 걸 끝내 안 갚았는데 둘 다 그 얘기를 그냥 안 꺼내게 된 거야. 그러니까 내가 안 된다고 하면 그동안 내가 계속 마음속으로 세고 있었다고 말하는 셈이지. 그렇다고 빌려주면 일 년 내내 속으로 꿍하게 있을 거고. 문자를 네 번이나 써 놨는데 하나도 못 보냈어.
sentences.text: My brother asked me for money again, and it's not that I don't have it, it's that he never paid me back last time and we both just stopped bringing it up. So if I say no, I'm basically telling him I've been keeping count this whole time. And if I say yes I'm going to be quietly annoyed about it for a year. I've typed out four different texts and I haven't sent any of them.

alts.text: So my brother hit me up for money again, and it's not that I don't have it, it's that he never paid me back last time and we both just quit mentioning it. If I say no, I'm basically telling him I've been keeping count this whole time. And if I say yes I'm gonna be quietly annoyed about it for a year. I've typed out four different texts and sent exactly none of them.

My brother has asked me for money again, and it is not that I do not have it. It is that he never repaid me last time and we both simply stopped mentioning it. If I decline, I am effectively telling him that I have been keeping count all along. If I agree, I will be quietly resentful about it for a year. I have composed four different messages and have not sent any of them.

sentences.note: **keeping count** 는 갚았는지 안 갚았는지 마음속으로 계속 세고 있었다는 뜻입니다. **quietly annoyed** 는 겉으로 말은 안 하면서 속으로만 계속 짜증이 나 있는 상태를 가리킵니다.
sentences.situation: 친구한테 고민 상담하면서 결론은 못 내리기

reviewed: 1번 한국어: garage 를 "창고"로 옮겼는데 창고는 물건 두는 광이고 차를 두는 곳은 "차고"입니다. 차고로 고쳤습니다.
3번 한국어: 영어는 they replaced her heater 라 집주인 쪽에서 갈아 준 것인데, 한국어가 "자기 집 온수기를 갈았다"로 되어 있어 아래층 사람이 직접 간 것처럼 읽힙니다. "온수기를 갈아 줬다고"로 고쳤습니다.
3번 formal: beat it 은 구어라 격식체에 섞이면 말투가 어긋납니다. finish before it runs out 으로 바꿨습니다(뜻은 그대로).
4번 casual: which 와 that 이 겹쳐 한 번 듣고 걸립니다. 문장을 끊어 "I'll go in the morning. Yeah, I say that every time." 으로 다듬었습니다.
